issues.legal_issue: A statutory direction to deduct income tax paid in respect of income from a particular source does not include super-tax charged on the taxpayer’s total income.
material_facts: Compensation for the acquired proprietary rights was calculated by multiplying the estate’s net income, determined under statutory rules, by a specified factor.
The rules allowed deduction of the average income tax paid in respect of income from a particular source.

The compensation authority deducted super-tax as well as income tax, although super-tax was charged on total income and could not be attributed to that particular source under the applicable tax rules.
The affected proprietor challenged the deduction, and the dispute reached the Court on appeal from the decision granting relief.
issues.conclusion: Super-tax was not deductible under the rule, because the rule referred to income tax paid in respect of income from the particular source and did not include super-tax charged on total income.
issues.legal_principle: The court construed the statutory language in context: the legislature referred to income tax but omitted super-tax, despite their being distinct duties under the Income-tax Act. The source-specific qualification also excluded super-tax, which was charged on total income and could not legally be apportioned to income from the specified source. The court considered the distinction between the taxes reflected in the Income-tax Act, including sections 3, 4, 6 and 55–58, and the compensation provisions in section 8 and Schedule I, rules 2(2)(c) and 8. It noted Lord Sumner’s statement in Brooks v. Commissioner of Inland Revenue that super-tax was a new tax notwithstanding its description as an additional duty of income tax; it found the reasoning in Bates, In re: Selmes v. Bates helpful and more pertinent, and distinguished Reckitt, In re: Reckitt v. Reckitt on its different wording and context.

rule.if: compensation_net_income_case and deduction_tied_to_specific_source and tax_charged_on_total_income and tax_not_attributable_to_specific_source

predicates.compensation_net_income_case: The proceeding concerns compensation calculated by determining a person’s net income under a statutory scheme.
predicates.deduction_tied_to_specific_source: The applicable calculation permits deduction of tax paid in respect of income from a particular source.
predicates.tax_charged_on_total_income: The disputed tax is charged on the taxpayer’s total income rather than separately on income from each source.
predicates.tax_not_attributable_to_specific_source: The tax rules provide no legally available way to attribute the disputed tax to income from the particular source.

issues.definition: When compensation is calculated using a source-specific tax deduction, a tax charged on total income and not attributable to that source is not deductible.
